verdicts.why: Describes the field-specific sense the gloss gives, explains its force by borrowing the weight of 'cannot read', and the negative charge and the 'musically illiterate' example both fit.
Flat report of knowledge not gained by study, in a field or generally, matches the gloss exactly and the neutral charge is plausible.
Locates the lack in schooling rather than mind, which is what 'lacking in schooling' says; a mild negative is consistent with the note's own 'mild'.
Reads the informer role and its stain straight out of the gloss 'act as an informer'; example and negative charge fit.

The gloss builds the excess into the word ('enlarge beyond bounds or the truth'), but the note says it 'only says something was made bigger' and puts the fault outside the word, which describes the plain make-larger sense and drives an implausible neutral charge.
Planting a false belief seen as a breach of trust matches 'cause someone to believe an untruth' and the negative charge.
Overstating past limits or truth with the real size implied smaller is the gloss; example fits and negative is plausible.
Formal register label plus the duty-resting-on-someone reading matches 'morally binding or necessary'; neutral is plausible.
Scorn at elegance put on for show is exactly 'pretentiously elegant'; the restaurant example and negative charge fit.
Crisp, efficient pace winning approval fits 'quick and energetic' and the positive charge; the neighbour contrast stays inside the word.
Intensifying push toward a rush fits the gloss and the 'rattling rate' example; positive is plausible for an approving intensifier.
Plain report of excitement and interest without judging desert matches the gloss; examples and positive charge fit.
Keeps the contest/contestant restriction of the gloss and describes the word's blame on the pairing; negative fits.
Flat denial rather than complaint is a tone claim that fits the gloss and the neutral charge.
Better-than-even chance framed as advantage matches the gloss and the 'odds-on favorite' example; positive is plausible.
Pointing at the equalising that was not done is a fair reading of 'not caused to be equal'; neutral fits.
Names the literal method of marking trees and judges nothing, which is the gloss; 'blaze a trail' fits and neutral is plausible.
Lifting something into notice matches 'make conspicuous or noteworthy'; the Austen examples use that sense and positive is plausible.
Light, blame-free colouring on a complete lack matches the gloss and 'innocent of literary merit'; the positive sign is plausible as the gentlest word in the lacking family.
Absence treated as shortfall rather than fact fits 'nonexistent' with the appetite example, and negative is plausible.
Unintended slip that gives the teller away is exactly 'reveal unintentionally'; negative is plausible.
Telling framed as a breach of intended secrecy fits the gloss and the negative charge.
Stripping cover off something kept back for a reason fits the gloss; both Austen examples are about publicly revealing hidden character and negative fits.
Makes the anonymous teller the point, which is all 'tell anonymously' gives; neutral is plausible for that bare gloss.
Buried-and-dug-up framing fits making hidden information public; neutral is plausible.
Neutral base word leaving nothing to work out matches the gloss and its examples.
Covers both halves of the gloss (unspoken and inherent) and contrasts a neighbour within the word; neutral fits.
Differentiates the phrase from its neighbours by its need for a complement, a fact about the word itself; neutral fits the gloss, though 'the meaning' is loose phrasing for whatever is inherent.
